text:
maya: Heads-up — a customer flagged that their CSV exports from the Console audit view are missing actor_ip and actor_email for service principals. Seen in prod and staging. Anyone hit this?

ahn: Can you paste a sample header/row so we can see what's missing?

maya: sure, here's the header from the export:
```
timestamp,actor_id,actor_type,action,target,actor_identifier,resource_kms_key
```
and a sample row (service principal):
```
2026-03-10T12:02:03Z,sp-1234,service_principal,grant,model-deploy,sp-1234,
```
Notice actor_ip and actor_email are absent.

julian: We rolled schema v2 last month which consolidated actor_email into actor_identifier to support external ids. That should have been backward-compatible but sounds like the Console export transformation didn't map for service_principals specifically.

elle: Also, per compliance, emails can be masked by KMS-based PII redaction if the caller lacks export_pii permission. Are these customers in a tenant with pii_export disabled? @maya :eyes:

maya: I checked — customer org has export_pii enabled. This looks like a transformation bug rather than masking. The export UI shows the columns in headers, but downstream CSV misses fields when the actor_type == service_principal.

sre_lead: Could this be a chunking/pagination bug during streaming export? If the serializer assumes fields from first page and later pages skip columns, we might drop columns when merging chunks.

ahn: plausible. The streaming export code path does incremental writes. If a chunk writer uses a different schema set, the CSV writer could omit columns. We had a similar bug in metrics ingestion.

security-bot: preflight-export-check: failed — export-validator returned schema-consistency-warning for job 0x7c3a. See run 2026-03-10T12:05:20Z.

julian: We should add an explicit "audit_schema_version" header to all exported artifacts to make debugging easier (and to keep file-level schema for downstream tooling). Suggest: `Audit-Schema: audit_v2` and include a JSON metadata sidecar for streaming exports.

elle: +1 on schema header. Also propose a Console UX change: when the export would drop PII columns due to RBAC or transform, show a non-blocking warning in the modal: "Some columns may be omitted due to role-based redaction or service principal mapping — see link". Saves support tickets.

maya: strong +1. For immediate triage: can infra spin up a repro with a service_principal actor and run the streaming export locally? I can hand off an example org.

ahn: I can repro it in staging. Quick triage plan:
1) run export with actor_type=service_principal and compare chunk schemas
2) add logging in csv chunk writer for omitted columns
3) validate whether transform step (email -> identifier) nulls value for sp

sre_lead: Also add a test that simulates mix of human+service_principal rows across pages.

julian: For longer term, two changes:
- keep schema header in artifact and attach `schema_version` to the stream
- make the CSV writer schema-first (emit header based on union of all fields seen in job)

elle: I'll draft a short RFC for the Console warning text and export UX affordance. Will include copy for the modal and an admin checkbox: "Include PII columns (requires export_pii permission)".

maya: awesome. Who's owning the bug fix?

ahn: I'll take the first pass on repro + logging. julian can follow with writer fix. elle will own UX/RFC. I'll open a ticket and link here.

maya: thanks — please add the staging link and the failing export job id in the ticket. @security-bot can you attach the preflight log to the ticket when it's created?

security-bot: ack — will attach preflight-export-check logs when ticket is created. :white_check_mark:

maya: cool, tagging @compliance FYI. I'll follow up with customer once we have a repro and a short mitigation (manual transform to backfill email column if needed). :thumbsup:
